claims.text: The initial material is nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 with equiaxed grains of approximately 70 nm.
The initial films are produced by magnetron sputtering.
Replacing 5 at.% Cr with 5 at.% V will favor a more homogeneous BCC solid solution.
Increasing V content will enhance V-dependent chemical short-range order.
Enhanced chemical short-range order will produce a more uniform elemental distribution in the BCC matrix.
Increasing V will make vacancy and self-interstitial mobilities more similar.
The altered defect mobilities will suppress excessive defect clustering.
A more uniform elemental distribution will reduce segregation leading to Cr-V-rich precipitates.
Increasing V will improve irradiation-defect recombination.
Improved defect recombination will produce fewer large interstitial clusters.
Fewer large interstitial clusters will reduce the number of precipitate-nucleation sites.
W38Ta36Cr10V16 will show significantly reduced or suppressed Cr-V-rich precipitation after irradiation to 8 dpa at 1073 K relative to W38Ta36Cr15V11.
W38Ta36Cr10V16 will show lower irradiation-induced hardening than W38Ta36Cr15V11.
W38Ta36Cr10V16 will retain a nanocrystalline BCC structure after irradiation to 8 dpa at 1073 K.
Replacing Cr with V will preserve high radiation tolerance.
Replacing Cr with V will preserve practical manufacturability.
Baseline W38Ta36Cr15V11 develops Cr-V-rich precipitates after irradiation to 8 dpa at 1073 K.
Precipitation in baseline W38Ta36Cr15V11 is accompanied by increased hardening.
Prior work in simpler W-Ta-V systems indicates that increased V suppresses segregation.
Prior work in simpler W-Ta-V systems indicates that increased V improves defect recombination.

contradictions.description: The intervention is framed as preserving the baseline alloy's low hardening, whereas the baseline field states that irradiation produces increased hardening. These could be reconciled only by defining whether the increase is negligible in magnitude, which is not done.
The hypothesis claims preservation of practical bulk manufacturability, but the boundary says effects in bulk samples remain unestablished and the proposed experiment tests only sputtered thin films.
